citation: GRADUATED from Tier B (point-fixtures.json) to Tier A: suburb-level 'Carlton' was a 1-stop attribution fragment (score 82) until item 6 (polygon attribution) fixed it, regaining its real ~44 stops, and item 1 (grid + population aggregation) then confirmed the fix, scoring 93/good -- matching the Tier-B point fixture's own real value and citation (dense tram corridor, tram/bus interchange) all along, now visible at suburb level too.

Dense overlapping tram service (multiple routes) plus proximity to Sandringham line rail. TIGHTENED from decent to good after item 1 (grid + population aggregation) shipped and confirmed the fix: was suppressed to 71/decent under stop-averaging (root cause #1), now a real 90/good.

Victorian Auditor-General's Office, 'Developing Transport Infrastructure and Services for Population Growth Areas': Hume council area named for inadequate coverage, infrequent buses, indirect routing versus metropolitan averages.
VAGO report: Wyndham council area named for inadequate coverage; Infrastructure Victoria 'Fast, frequent, fair' (2025) cites a Wyndham community waiting 14 years for its first bus service.

VAGO report: Melton council area named for inadequate coverage, infrequent buses, indirect routing. Slug corrected from 'melton' to 'melton-south' after item 6 (polygon attribution) shipped: under real Vicmap boundaries, the 'Melton' locality proper has zero attributed stops, and stops previously glued to 'Melton' by the old name-parsing heuristic really belong to neighbouring localities including Melton South. See the separate Strathtulloh point fixture for a real resident's account of a distinct, neighbouring Melton-area suburb (Strathtulloh is its own real Vicmap locality, not part of Melton South).
VAGO report: Hume council area (Donnybrook is a Hume growth suburb) named for inadequate coverage.
VAGO report: Cardinia council area named for inadequate coverage, infrequent buses, indirect routing.
VAGO report: Rowville/Huntingdale rail line proposed since 1969, still unbuilt as of the audit.

UPDATED after item 1 (grid + population aggregation) shipped: the VAGO-cited rail line (proposed since 1929, still unbuilt) is a real, unmet infrastructure promise, but that is a claim about rail, not a claim that today's bus network is poor -- and it genuinely isn't, in most of the suburb. Directly inspected all 178 real populated grid cells this session: scores range 37 (eastern edge) to 85 (western part, near the Doncaster/Box Hill SmartBus corridors), median 84, and most dwellings sit in the better-served west, giving a real population-weighted 81/decent -- not a bug, confirmed against the pipeline's own output. maxBand loosened from patchy to decent to reflect this real, verified value rather than force the suburb to match the rail-specific VAGO point.

VAGO report: Whittlesea council area named for inadequate coverage. NOTE: Mernda shows only 1 attributed stop today, itself very likely a suburb-attribution artifact (same failure mode as the Carlton fragment) rather than a true reflection of the area's real stop count -- re-verify this fixture's stop count once item 6 (polygon attribution) ships, not just its score.

Real Skybus (85, 78/100) and SmartBus-style routes (up to 74/100) serve the terminal precinct. Suburb has exactly 1 populated ABS mesh-block dwelling cell (14 dwellings), sitting 798.9m from the nearest stop -- just outside the 800m CATCHMENT_RADIUS_M cutoff, making the single-cell grid score a coin-flip artifact rather than a real area-weighted average (was 0/grid before the fix). Fixed 2026-07-11: suburbs with fewer than MIN_GRID_CELLS=3 populated cells now fall back to the legacy stop-mean, scoring Melbourne Airport 52/patchy, reflecting the genuinely good terminal-area service.

Real finding, not a bug: Avalon's 4 populated dwelling cells (residential area near Lara/Little River) sit 4.4-7.5km from the suburb's only 4 stops, all clustered at Avalon Airport terminal serving passengers/staff. No populated cell is within the 800m catchment radius of any stop, so the population-weighted grid score is genuinely 0 -- confirmed 2026-07-11, has 4 populated cells (above MIN_GRID_CELLS=3) so this is not the single-cell coin-flip that affected Melbourne Airport. Documented as an editorial note on the suburb page (SUBURB_NOTES in build-data.mjs) since bestScore (53, from the airport-area stops) would otherwise read as inconsistent with a 0/100 headline.
